title: Anima CLI configuration (anima.json)
description: Project-level configuration for the Anima CLI (`anima` / `am`). Place it at the project root or any ancestor directory — the CLI walks up from the current working directory. Secret references are resolved at the edge by `anima vault exec|proxy|agent`; plaintext values never live in this file.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema for editor completion and validation.

secrets.description: Map of logical name → secret reference. Keys are the variable names exposed to the consuming command (environment-variable style by convention, e.g. GH_TOKEN).

secretRef.description: A declarative pointer to a secret, resolved at execution time. Never a plaintext value.

animaRef.description: Fetch from the Anima vault by credential id + dotted field path. Resolution uses the single-use vault-token flow, so every access is a distinct audit-log entry.

credentialId.description: Vault credential id, e.g. "cred_abc123" — from the Anima console or `anima vault list`.

field.description: Dotted path into the credential object, e.g. "login.password" or "apiKey.key".

agentId.description: Optional agent id override (useful for master-key access across agents). Defaults to the CLI's authenticated agent.

envRef.description: Resolve from a local environment variable. The CLI refuses to run if the variable is unset or empty — no silent fallback.

name.description: Environment variable name — uppercase letters, digits, and underscores; must start with a letter.

execRef.description: Run a trusted binary (no shell) and capture stdout as the secret. 15-second timeout, 1 MiB output cap, trailing newline trimmed.

command.description: Absolute path or bare name of a trusted binary. No shell expansion; whitespace and shell metacharacters (; & | < > $ ` \) are rejected.

args.description: Arguments passed to the binary — each element is a literal argv slot, no globbing.

passEnv.description: Environment variable names passed through to the subprocess. Everything else is stripped (PATH is always included so the binary can be found).

cwd.description: Optional working directory for the subprocess.
